title: The Long Run

pages.title: The Familiar Trail
pages.caption: In October 2026, Mantas went into the Vilnius woods for his usual long run. During the week he built a company and led its technology team; out here, the next kilometre was enough to occupy him. He knew this path by its bends and roots. At the first climb, he slowed. A pine lay across the trail, its stump cleanly sawn. Pale sawdust still rested on the damp ground. Beyond it, two muddy tire tracks followed the narrow path into the trees. Mantas stopped beside the cut. Someone had brought machinery onto a trail he had run for years.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: That wasn't here last week.

pages.continuity_note: Opening scene establishes the fixed 2026 Vilnius trail-run premise and the protagonist; a newly felled tree interrupts his familiar route.
pages.summary: In October 2026, Mantas, a Lithuanian entrepreneur and tech executive, sets out for his routine long run in the forests of Vilnius. A freshly sawn pine blocks his familiar narrow trail, and muddy tire tracks lead onward into the woods. He stops to examine the cut and wonders who brought machinery onto the path.

pages.title: The Buried Wheel
pages.caption: Mantas picked his way around the pine and followed the muddy tracks. Fifty metres beyond the bend, he found their source: a green forestry tractor, its front wheel sunk deep into a wet rut, with a short trailer of cut logs behind it. The man beside it looked more embarrassed than surprised to see him. He pointed back along the trail, then at the wheel. Mantas had come out to give his mind a rest from other people's problems. He looked at the mud, the man's empty hands, and the quiet machine. His pace no longer mattered.

dialogue.speaker: Forestry worker
dialogue.text: I cut that pine this morning. Thought I could get the trailer through.

dialogue.speaker: Forestry worker
dialogue.text: Can you help me call someone?

pages.continuity_note: Mantas walks around the fallen pine and follows its muddy tire tracks a short distance. He finds the worker who says he cut the tree, now beside a stuck tractor and timber trailer.
pages.summary: In October 2026, Mantas, a Lithuanian entrepreneur and tech executive, sets out for his routine long run in the forests of Vilnius. A freshly sawn pine blocks his familiar narrow trail, with muddy tire tracks beyond it. Mantas walks around the trunk and follows the tracks fifty metres around a bend to a green forestry tractor with a short timber trailer. Its front wheel is stuck in a wet rut. An uninjured older forestry worker says he cut the pine that morning and thought he could get the trailer through. He asks Mantas to help him call someone; Mantas pauses his run to respond.

pages.title: A Call Through the Trees
pages.caption: Mantas pulled his phone from the vest pocket and asked for the number. The man introduced himself as Jonas, then slowly recited his colleague’s digits. A faint voice answered on the second attempt. Mantas described the bend, the loaded trailer and the sunken front wheel. Jonas leaned closer, his worried expression easing as he heard the reply. Another tractor could reach them in about twenty minutes. Mantas looked at the churned-up track. His planned run could wait; for now, they had someone coming.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Tell him we’ll wait here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: He knows the track. About twenty minutes.

pages.continuity_note: Mantas answers the forestry worker’s request by calling his colleague. The worker introduces himself as Jonas. Help is arranged while both men and the loaded tractor remain at the same muddy bend.
pages.summary: In October 2026, Mantas, a Lithuanian entrepreneur and tech executive, sets out for his routine long run in the forests of Vilnius. Mantas follows the tracks fifty metres around a bend to a green forestry tractor with a loaded short timber trailer. Its front wheel is stuck in a wet rut and its engine is off. An uninjured older forestry worker says he cut the pine that morning and thought he could get the trailer through, then asks for help calling someone. The worker introduces himself as Jonas and gives Mantas his colleague’s number. Mantas gets through on his phone and explains their location and the problem. The colleague knows the track and can bring another tractor in about twenty minutes. Mantas has paused his run to wait with Jonas; recovery has not yet occurred.

pages.title: The First Pull
pages.caption: Twenty minutes later, the low rumble of another tractor reached the bend. Jonas climbed back into his cab while his colleague attached a tow cable and took position on the firmer part of the track. Mantas put his phone away and waited on the verge. The cable tightened. For a moment the green tractor only rocked; then its muddy front wheel began to rise against the edge of the rut. Jonas held the steering wheel steady, the pine logs still upright behind him. Mantas watched the orange vest through the cab window. There was movement now, and room to let the workers finish.
pages.continuity_note: The colleague arrives by the forest track about twenty minutes after the successful phone call. A slow tow begins to lift the same green tractor’s front wheel at the same bend; full recovery has not yet been shown.

pages.title: Firm Ground
pages.caption: The front wheel clears the lip of the rut. Jonas keeps the green tractor straight while his colleague draws the loaded trailer onto the firmer stretch ahead. Only when the trailer’s last wheels are clear do they stop. The tow cable falls slack against the leaves. From the open cab door, Jonas gives Mantas a relieved thumbs-up. Mantas has checked his watch; now he answers with a wave from the mossy verge. The delay has cooled his legs, and he shifts his weight, ready to start again. Behind the bend, the sawn pine still lies across the footpath.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Thank you for staying.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Glad it worked. I’ll get moving.

pages.continuity_note: Immediately after the slow tow begins to lift the front wheel, the colleague completes the recovery onto firm track; both tractors stop with the trailer still coupled and upright.

Jonas opens his cab door and gives Mantas a relieved thumbs-up, and Mantas answers with a wave after checking his watch and prepares to resume the paused run. The sawn pine remains across the footpath behind the bend.

pages.title: Back into Stride
pages.caption: Around the bend, Mantas finds the pine exactly where he left it. Pale sawdust lies beside the stump, and the trunk still cuts across his familiar path. He slows to a walk and follows a short strip of firm moss around the sawn end, watching where he places his feet. Beyond the timber, the trail opens again between the birches. He takes an easy first stride, letting the rhythm return. His long run has acquired an unexpected pause, a phone call and two new faces; now it has its next ordinary step.
pages.continuity_note: The inspected picture shows the same uninjured Mantas in his established running kit, jogging on the clear path after passing the pine’s pale sawn end. The fallen trunk still blocks the trail behind him, with the stump and fresh sawdust beside it. This follows his farewell and the return fifty metres around the established bend; the recovered machinery remains out of view.

pages.title: A Smaller Loop
pages.caption: Several minutes beyond the fallen pine, Mantas reaches the familiar fork. His breathing has settled back into its easy rhythm, but the watch brings the morning into focus: helping Jonas has used twenty minutes of the run. With his wrist still raised, he decides to take the shorter return loop on the left. The other branch climbs between roots and stones. There is no need to win the time back by pushing harder over them. The forest still offers a good run; it will simply be a smaller one today.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Short loop today.

pages.continuity_note: Mantas has jogged for several minutes along the clear familiar trail after bypassing the sawn pine. At a familiar fork he chooses the shorter return loop because the forestry recovery delayed him about twenty minutes.

pages.title: Back at the Edge
pages.caption: Fifteen minutes after the fork, the trees opened onto the familiar trailhead. Mantas eased into a walk, then stopped beside the low wooden railing and took a drink, his free hand resting on the damp timber. The shorter loop had brought him back without a hurried finish. His legs felt the wet ground, but his breathing was settling. The morning had cost him twenty unexpected minutes; it had also left two workers and their loaded trailer safely on firm track. He let that be enough for the moment. First, water and a quiet walk out of the trees.
pages.continuity_note: Mantas follows the chosen shorter return loop at a comfortable pace and reaches its familiar trailhead about fifteen minutes after the fork. He finishes the adjusted run and pauses for water; the forestry site stays behind him.

He pauses by its low wooden railing to drink from one hydration flask before walking out.

pages.title: Back in Reach
pages.caption: Mantas pushes the flask back into its pocket and leaves the railing behind. A few metres farther on, the gravel widens toward the quiet street beyond the trees. His phone vibrates. It is Rūta from the company, asking whether he can join the team before noon to look through their signup flow. He keeps an easy walking pace and listens. The run is finished, even if it was shorter than planned; there is no need to hurry the last few steps. He agrees to the review and keeps walking toward the street, carrying the morning’s interruption back into an ordinary working day.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta (by phone)
dialogue.text: Can we review the signup flow before noon?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. I’ll come back and look at it with you.

pages.continuity_note: Inspected the saved picture: Mantas is walking at the same woodland trailhead exit, the familiar railing recedes behind him, both flasks are restored to the black vest, and his right hand holds a phone to his right ear. pages.title: A Fresh Attempt
pages.caption: Before noon, Mantas is back at the company’s Vilnius office. His running vest hangs on the chair as he leans over the table beside Rūta. She points to the signup flow on the laptop: its second step requests the same contact details again. Rather than jumping straight to a fix, Mantas proposes following the whole route as a new visitor. The interruption in the forest has used up his spare time; this meeting will have to stay focused. They begin with the first screen.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: It asks for the same details twice.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s try it from the beginning.

pages.continuity_note: Later the same October morning, Mantas returns normally to the company’s Vilnius office and starts the signup review he agreed to during the trailhead phone call. pages.title: Carry It Forward
pages.caption: Rūta enters a fresh set of test details and advances through signup. The next screen opens with the same fields empty. Going back, they find the original entries still sitting in the first step. The effort has been repeated because the information has not followed the visitor. Mantas watches her return to the second screen. They agree on a small, concrete change: carry the details forward, and let the next step ask only for something new. Before changing anything, Rūta will record the example so the team can reproduce it and check the result.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: It kept them back there. It just asks again here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Carry them forward. Then test the whole path again.

pages.title: The Reproducible Case
pages.caption: Rūta records the route through signup, the empty fields they found, and what should happen instead. Beside the laptop, Mantas sketches two simple steps joined by an arrow. The details already entered belong to the same person all the way through. They add one more check: going back and forward must not lose those entries either. With the example and expected behavior written down, the problem is ready for the team to change and test. The sketch settles the intended flow; the software still needs the work.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Steps, result, expected behavior. It’s recorded.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: And check going back, then forward again.

pages.caption: About twenty minutes later, Mantas turns the laptop toward himself and makes the agreed change in a local preview. dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The details are here. Now go back.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then forward again, with the new field filled.

pages.caption: Mantas filled the additional field, went back, and changed one contact detail. When he moved forward again, the correction followed him and the new entry was still there. dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The entries stayed. The whole path passed.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas

pages.caption: Before noon, Mantas asks a teammate to give the small change a fresh look. Darius joins them at the table, examines the change and follows Rūta’s recorded steps himself. dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: The change is clear, and the checks pass. Approved.

pages.title: Into the Live Flow
pages.caption: With Darius’s review complete, Mantas releases the small change. A few minutes later, the release finishes and Rūta opens a fresh signup on the live service. She enters the contact details once, moves forward, then returns to correct one of them. On the next screen, the correction is there and the additional entry remains. The final confirmation appears without another request for the same details. Darius stays with them for the check, and Rūta points to the result beside her open notebook. The morning’s interruption has become a finished repair. Mantas rests his hands on the table, ready to leave the meeting room.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The release is complete.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The live check passed. We’re done.

pages.continuity_note: This follows Darius’s completed independent review in the same meeting room. Mantas releases the approved change, and Rūta verifies the existing acceptance checks on the live service. The signup repair is now complete.

pages.title: The Footpath
pages.caption: With the live signup checked, the meeting breaks up. Rūta closes the laptop and Darius heads out. Mantas gathers his vest from the chair and retrieves his phone. The morning has left one practical question unanswered: the pine still lies across a route he knows other runners use. He calls Jonas. The worker says they are cutting the trunk into sections now that the tractor is free, and promises to call when the footpath is clear. Mantas thanks him. The office repair is finished; the woodland job is still underway. For now, he will keep using the safe way around the cut end.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: How is the footpath looking?

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: We’re cutting the trunk into sections. I’ll call when it’s clear.

pages.continuity_note: Minutes after the successful live signup check, the meeting ends. Mantas retrieves the phone and vest shown in the previous picture and follows up with Jonas about the known pine obstruction; removal remains unconfirmed.

pages.title: The Open Path
pages.caption: Later that morning, Jonas finishes moving the cut pine onto the moss beside the path. The last section rests with the others; only pale sawdust remains on the tread. He pauses beside the fresh stump and looks along the route that had stopped Mantas earlier. There is room to pass freely now. Jonas takes out his phone and keeps the promise he made during their call. The tractor recovery had got the timber moving; clearing the footpath finishes the job for the people who use the forest on foot.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: The path is clear now, Mantas. All the sections are off the trail.

pages.continuity_note: Jonas’s last report established that the obstructing pine was being cut into sections. Later the same morning he finishes moving those sections off the tread and calls Mantas as promised; the reopened footpath is shown directly.

pages.title: A Promise Kept
pages.caption: At the meeting-room doorway, Mantas pauses with his vest over one arm. Jonas’s promised call has arrived: the pine sections are off the tread, and the familiar footpath is open again. Mantas listens, then thanks him for following through. Across the table, Rūta gathers the notes beside the closed laptop. The signup repair has passed its live check; the obstruction that interrupted the run has been cleared too. Neither task needs another urgent decision. Mantas lowers his shoulders. He can change out of his running clothes, then join Rūta for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Thanks for calling, Jonas. I’m glad the path is clear.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Lunch after you change?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. I’ll meet you downstairs.

pages.title: Time to Look Around
pages.caption: By noon, Mantas had changed upstairs and found Rūta at the café below the office. The soup was hot, and for the first time that morning neither of them had a screen between them. Rūta asked about the delay on his run. He described the stuck tractor, the patient tow and Jonas’s call after clearing the path. Beyond the window, the autumn trees caught her attention. She had lived in Vilnius for years without learning many of its forest paths. They agreed on a weekend walk along his familiar loop, with time to look around instead of watching the pace.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Will you show me that trail this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Of course. We can walk the short loop.

pages.continuity_note: A little later the same day, Mantas has changed as planned and met Rūta downstairs for lunch. His account of the resolved forest incident leads naturally to their agreed weekend walk.

pages.title: Room to Walk
pages.caption: That weekend, Mantas and Rūta set out on the short forest loop they had discussed over lunch. A few minutes into the walk, he stopped beside the pale stump. The pine sections lay on the moss, well clear of the tread, just as Jonas had promised. Rūta looked from the cut wood to the open path. Here, the morning’s interruption was already becoming an ordinary part of the landscape. Mantas had passed this place at running pace many times. With someone beside him, there was time to notice it. They would take the rest of the loop slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: This is where the pine blocked the path.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Now there’s room for both of us.

pages.caption: A few minutes beyond the cleared pine, they take the familiar left-hand return branch. Rūta stops beside a birch and lifts a hand. A woodpecker clings to the pale trunk, tapping in short bursts. Mantas looks up. He has passed this stretch often enough to know every turn, yet cannot remember watching a bird here. They stay still until the tapping resumes. The loop is the same one he runs; at walking pace, with someone else's attention to follow, it has more in it than the route on his watch.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Listen. Up there.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: I usually run straight past.

pages.title: At Walking Pace
pages.caption: After their pause by the birch, they carry on. The familiar return path takes them through the pines and back to the woodland edge, with no reason to hurry. About half an hour later, they reach the small trailhead clearing together. Mantas gestures back toward the woods. On his weekday run, this had been a place to finish, drink and check the time. Today the same loop has held a cleared passage, a bird he would have missed, and an easy conversation. Rūta smiles beside him as they share the thought.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Same loop. A different morning.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: We had time to notice it.

pages.caption: As they turn to leave the clearing, a woman arriving with a walking pole asks whether there is a short route from here. Mantas points along the open path and explains where the familiar left branch brings her back to the trailhead. For once, his directions include room to linger. Rūta smiles and adds that the loop need not take the same amount of time for everyone. The woman listens, looking from his hand to the trees. Their own walk is finished; its discoveries have become something they can pass on.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Take the left branch at the fork. It brings you back here.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Leave yourself a little time to stop.

dialogue.speaker: Walker
dialogue.text: That sounds just right. Thank you.

pages.title: A Pace to Keep
pages.caption: The woman turned toward the trees and set off with her pole. Mantas and Rūta followed the path toward the exit, leaving the bench and the forest loop behind them. Their morning had ended without a hurry. Rūta suggested trying the same small pause during a workday: a short walk at lunch, with enough time to notice where they were. Mantas agreed. They did not choose a route or a day yet. For now, they kept walking together through the fallen leaves.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Shall we try a short walk at lunch next week?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. Let’s make time for it.

pages.title: Ten Minutes Outside
pages.caption: At noon the following Monday, Rūta met Mantas by the office door. They chose a ten-minute loop through the small public garden nearby, leaving enough of their break for lunch afterward. At the garden entrance, Mantas slipped his phone into his pocket. Rūta opened a hand as she suggested a circuit through the autumn trees. The forest was farther away today, but the slower pace was close at hand: a few fallen leaves, a bench in the sun, and a path they could follow without hurrying. They began the loop together.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Around the garden and back?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. We have ten minutes.

pages.caption: The garden gate came back into view as their ten-minute circuit ended. On the last curve, Mantas glanced at his watch. A long run required planning; this little circuit had fitted into the space they already had.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Ten minutes. We have time for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Let’s go.

pages.caption: A few minutes after leaving the garden, they found a window table in the nearby café. Their soup was warm, and the office was still within an easy walk. Mantas left his phone in his pocket. The ten-minute circuit had asked for no rearrangement of the day; it had simply given them something else to look at before lunch. Rūta set her scarf over the back of her chair. They could fit another short walk into Wednesday’s break, they agreed, and still leave time to eat.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Same ten minutes on Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. Let’s keep the time for lunch, too.

dialogue.text: Wednesday, same time?

pages.title: One Thing First
pages.caption: Upstairs, their coats went onto hooks and lunch gave way to a table covered in the afternoon’s work. Darius had laid out three improvements for the next release. Mantas put his finger on the nearest card: a clearer explanation of what a new user should do after signing up. The other two could wait until this one had been tested. Rūta opened her notebook and wrote down the task. Their break had ended; the afternoon now had a starting point.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Which one goes first?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The next step after signup. Let’s make it clear.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I’ll bring the customer questions.

pages.continuity_note: After entering their Vilnius office following Monday lunch, Mantas and Rūta go upstairs, remove their outdoor layers and resume work with established teammate Darius by choosing one next-release task.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: They’re asking whether they’re finished—or whether they’ve missed a step.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Confirm the account first. Then show one useful next action.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Let’s see if someone new understands the sketch.

pages.title: The First Read
pages.caption: Before anyone turned the sketch into code, Rūta invited Lina from accounts to the table. Lina had never used the signup flow. Mantas set the page in front of her and let her examine it. The confirmation made sense immediately: her account was ready. The large button was less clear. In their draft notes, its proposed label was simply “Continue,” and Lina could not tell whether it opened the account or began another signup step. Rūta wrote down the question. A few quiet minutes had found something the three of them had overlooked.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: My account is ready. Does “Continue” open it, or is there another signup step?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s name where it takes you.

pages.continuity_note: A few minutes after Mantas sketches the untested welcome screen, Rūta brings in an unfamiliar accounts colleague for the planned comprehension check. Her question exposes ambiguous next-action wording; implementation is still deferred.

dialogue.text: Let’s check returning later next.

pages.title: Ten Minutes Kept
pages.caption: By Wednesday lunchtime, the garden path was scattered with yellow leaves. Mantas and Rūta had put on their jackets and come out for the walk they had promised over Monday’s soup. The released guidance task was finished; the two postponed improvements were still waiting at the office. A few steps into the loop, Rūta admitted that she had nearly stayed at her desk. dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I nearly stayed at my desk.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The list can wait ten minutes.

pages.caption: The path curved back to the garden gate. Mantas checked his watch: their ten minutes were up, and there was still time for lunch. Rūta gathered the ends of her scarf beside him. dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Same time next Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s keep the ten minutes.

pages.caption: A few minutes beyond the garden gate, they settled beside the café window with bowls of soup. Rūta brought up the two improvements they had left waiting on Monday. dialogue.text: Shall we look at the other two tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Bring the customer examples. Then we can choose.

pages.caption: They finished Wednesday’s lunch and returned to work within their break. On Thursday morning, Rūta brought the customer examples they had promised to review. Three described the same difficulty: once an account held several saved entries, finding an earlier one meant opening them in turn. A fourth asked for an exported overview. Export could wait; the search still had to earn its place.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: These three are trying to find something they already saved.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s test a search before we build it.

Once it has moved clear, he can carry on at the same easy pace.

Then a shower, breakfast, and the journey to the office. For now, he paused at the threshold before closing the door behind him.

pages.caption: The bus carried Mantas back into the working morning. pages.title: The Wet Pavement
pages.caption: By the end of Monday, the office had returned to its ordinary rhythm. Mantas finished his afternoon work, pulled on his olive jacket and walked to the nearby bus stop. Rain tapped the shelter roof and darkened the fallen leaves along the curb. He watched the water gather between them while he waited to go home. Tomorrow, he decided, he would look at the forest ground in daylight before choosing the length of his run. The weather outside the office could suggest caution; it could not tell him what lay on the trail.

pages.title: A Shorter Morning
pages.caption: By Tuesday daylight, the night’s rain had become a question he could answer with his feet. After sleep, breakfast and the journey to the woodland edge, Mantas stopped before starting his watch. A shallow puddle held the pale sky; wet leaves lay across the exposed roots. He set one shoe carefully at the edge and tested his footing. This first stretch was enough to make the longer run less appealing, though it told him nothing certain about the ground farther in. He chose the familiar short loop at an easy pace, ready to slow to a walk wherever the footing required it.

pages.caption: Beyond the first puddle, Mantas begins with short, unhurried strides. Rain has darkened the earth, but a narrow strip of firm ground still shows through the fallen leaves. He is moving comfortably now; that is enough for the opening minutes. The ground around the next curve will need its own look. For the moment, the familiar short loop gives him room to settle into the run.

pages.caption: Around the bend, the trail dipped and the rain had collected across its middle. Mantas shortened his stride, then let the jog become a walk. A strip of exposed earth remained along the inner edge, wide enough to use without stepping into the wet leaves beyond the path. He placed one orange shoe on it and looked ahead for the next foothold. The short loop would still be there if he took a few slower steps. For now, keeping his balance mattered more than keeping his pace.

The brief walk past the puddle had simply become part of the run. He let his breathing settle as he crossed the firm ground, still alone, with both flasks in his vest. Before leaving, he would take a drink.

Damp leaves lie flat on the firm ground; beyond the birches, the city is beginning its morning. The short loop has given him what he wanted today: movement, fresh air and enough time to notice his footing. He lets the pause last another moment before putting the flask away and heading out of the forest.

pages.title: Define the Work
pages.caption: With the maintenance recorded as complete, Darius returned to his own desk. Mantas opened the afternoon’s planning draft: a proposed support colleague. The document listed tools, but it said little about what the person would actually own. He drew a fresh outline in his notebook—answer routine questions, record uncertainty, and bring decisions to the responsible person. Rūta paused beside him with the draft. They agreed to make those boundaries clear before recruitment began. The verified search could keep doing its job while they worked out this different kind of responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s define the work before we advertise it.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And say where a question goes when they can’t answer it.

pages.title: A Clear Boundary
pages.caption: Mantas turned the broad idea of helping customers into a few concrete duties: record the exact question and the step that caused uncertainty, then answer from guidance the team had already checked. Rūta placed the draft beside his notebook and added a boundary. If the reported behavior was unclear, or the answer depended on a change, the support colleague would bring the details to the responsible teammate and arrange a follow-up. dialogue.text: The first job is to understand the question.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And know when to bring it to the team.

pages.caption: Rūta pulled up a chair and opened a fresh document. The agreed duties became a recruitment draft: listen carefully, write clear replies, use checked guidance and keep track of follow-ups. Mantas added a small exercise using fictional details. For a little while, the next thing to do was simply eat.

For now, there was only this small task to finish, then an evening to himself.

Under the lamp, he found his place and began to read. The warm windows across Vilnius were small against the deepening blue outside. There was no next decision waiting on this page, no reply to prepare before he turned it. Supper was finished, the day’s work was closed, and his phone stayed in the jacket in the hallway. For a while, the evening could move at the pace of a sentence.

Light from the kitchen still reached the chair; beyond the window, Vilnius glimmered blue and gold. His place in the book would wait. It was time to sleep.

Tomorrow could begin after a night’s sleep.

The folded clothes were still on the chair; the phone was still in the hallway jacket. Yesterday’s customer follow-up was closed. This morning could begin at an ordinary pace.

He set the hydration vest on a dry patch beside the sink and held the first flask beneath the tap; the second waited within reach. The familiar preparations gave the morning a shape: water first, then his phone from the hallway jacket, then the trail. He would take the woodland route at an easy pace. For now, he watched the flask fill.

The long run would begin gently. There was no need to spend the morning’s calm before he reached the trees.

A bus rolled toward him through the pale morning light. He stayed back from the kerb, watching it slow, while the city began its Friday around him.

He let his hands rest on his thighs and watched the morning light reach the upper windows. The familiar woodland lay ahead along the route. For now, the journey gave him a few quiet minutes before the long run.

pages.caption: The buildings thinned, and the familiar belt of woodland appeared beside the road. At the woodland-edge stop, Mantas stepped onto the pavement and followed the short pedestrian link to the trailhead. By his first easy strides, the bus was already moving away. Cool shade gathered beneath the birches and pines, while sunlight caught the gold leaves above him. He let the opening minutes stay gentle, giving his legs time to warm. Both flasks were filled; his phone and keys stayed zipped away. The long run had begun.

pages.title: Room to Pass
pages.caption: Beyond the curve, a cyclist was walking his bicycle up the narrow path. Mantas eased out of his jog and stepped onto firm moss beside the trail. The rider kept the wheels on the clear strip of earth, leaving the ferns undisturbed. They exchanged a brief nod as the bicycle came through. Mantas waited with his hands relaxed, ready to step back once the rear wheel had passed. A few quiet seconds gave them both room; his steady run could carry on from here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Cyclist
dialogue.text: Thanks.

pages.title: Back into Stride
pages.caption: Mantas waited until the bicycle’s rear wheel had passed, then stepped from the firm moss onto the clear trail. The cyclist continued uphill behind him. A few easy strides brought back the rhythm of the run: feet light on the leaf-strewn earth, breath even, eyes on the next stretch. He let the brief pause remain a pause, without trying to make up its seconds. Morning light reached between the pines as the path carried him farther along the longer circuit. There was room now to run at his own comfortable pace.

pages.title: The Homeward Bend
pages.caption: A few minutes beyond the cyclist, the path dipped toward a shallow stream. Mantas recognized the low wooden bridge: from here, the longer circuit would curve back toward the woodland edge. A thin shine of moisture lay across the planks. He let his stride shorten, then settled into a walk. The stream slipped quietly beneath him as he kept his steps measured. There was time to take this crossing at its own pace. Beyond the bridge, the clear path continued between the birches.
pages.continuity_note: After resuming his jog beyond the courteous cyclist pass, Mantas advances several minutes along the same longer circuit, reaches its stream footbridge and slows to walk on damp planks as the route bends homeward.

pages.title: The Far Bank
pages.caption: On the far bank, Mantas walked a few more steps until the damp planks were behind him. The return path was firm and clear, with enough room to find his comfortable rhythm again. He eased back into a jog. The little bridge receded between the trunks while the shallow stream followed its own course below the mossy bank. There was no reason to make up the seconds spent walking; he still had the rest of the familiar return trail ahead.

pages.title: The Last Stretch
pages.caption: About ten minutes beyond the stream, the trees began to thin and the return path opened into the familiar woodland-edge trailhead. Mantas let his final easy strides settle into a walk. The longer circuit was complete: a drink after the climb, careful steps over the wet ground, room for another trail user, and an unhurried crossing of the bridge. Now he could simply catch his breath. His flasks stayed secured in the vest; the bus home was the next part of the morning.

pages.title: The Homeward Bus
pages.caption: A few minutes of gentle walking settled Mantas’s breathing. He followed the pavement from the woodland edge to the bus stop, the morning light still low through the birches. When the bus drew in and stopped beside the curb, he stepped through the open door with a hand on the rail. The longer circuit was finished; there was no reason to hurry the journey home. His flasks stayed secured in the vest, and his phone and keys remained zipped away. Breakfast and a shower could wait until he reached his flat.

Now he lifted the vest onto its hook, both flasks still secured in their pockets. The phone could stay zipped away a little longer; his keys were on the shelf. The longer circuit was finished, and he had returned without hurrying the wet sections. A shower and breakfast were next, before the working day began.
